VibePascal v55 Linux x86_64 compiler -- -FU/-FE output directories are created
instead of aborting the build
Source commit: eae5d3e919 (merge of fix/output-dir-autocreate)
Compiler fix:  4d10b26fe772dfbd4992cbeb53f09028f7dfee4f
Parent release: v54 (b7d2d9676ecf1d7d8250cd460b9c48069920513e)
Built: 2026-09-10, native self-host fixpoint on x86_64-linux
ppcx64 md5:    19F526BD6BE0EC63FCA96C4D1B77E19D

Contents: bin/ppcx64 only -- a COMPILER-BINARY refresh meant to drop into an
existing VibePascal source/unit tree on Linux.  Only compiler/options.pas
changed between v54 and v55: no RTL change, no package change, no PPU format
change, so an existing v54 (or v53/v52) Linux unit set stays valid and the
utility binaries (ppudump/ppumove/fpcres/...) are unchanged and not re-shipped.

WHY THIS EXISTS, AND WHY IT IS LATE
  The fix shipped to Win64 as v55 on 2026-09-10 because that is where it was
  reported: the Win64 package's bin/fpc.cfg carries -FU./units/$FPCTARGET, so
  the very first compile after unpacking died before the user had written a
  line of their own code.  The Linux packages ship no fpc.cfg, so Linux users
  did NOT hit that first-run trap -- but the underlying compiler behaviour is
  not Windows-specific, and anyone on Linux who passes -FU or -FE explicitly
  hit exactly the same wall.  v54 and earlier refused; v55 creates the
  directory.  Shipping the fix only to Windows left that difference in place
  on five other platforms for no reason other than where the report came from.

CHANGE
  -FE and -FU name where the COMPILER writes, so both directories are now
  created up front, recursively, during option processing.  The existing
  "Path ... does not exist" diagnostic is reported only after creation has
  been TRIED and FAILED, so an impossible path (a component is a plain file,
  a read-only parent, a bad mount) still stops the build with the same
  message, now naming the directory.  One behaviour change: -FE on a missing
  directory used to error and now creates it; -FU never had that diagnostic
  at all, it failed later and more obscurely at object-write time.

VERIFIED ON THIS PLATFORM (x86_64-linux, native -- not emulated, not wine)
  A/B against the PUBLISHED pre-fix v54 Linux binary
  (dist/linux64/vibepascal-v54-b7d2d9676e-linux-x86_64-bin.tar.gz,
  ppcx64 md5 EB57AA4D7A3C1317CAF5921A6DDABF7B), same source, same config,
  same fresh directory, varying ONLY the compiler:
    -FUoutdir, outdir absent:  v54 -> exit 1, "Can't create object file:
                               outdir/hello.o (error code: 2)", outdir NOT
                               created.  v55 -> exit 0, outdir created,
                               hello linked and produced.
    -FEoutdir, outdir absent:  v54 -> exit 1, Error: Path "outdir/" does not
                               exist, outdir NOT created.  v55 -> exit 0,
                               outdir created, outdir/hello linked.
  The pre-fix control FAILS both corners, so this comparison can fail; an
  exit-0-either-way harness would have proved nothing.

  Carried from the v55 validation performed on this same binary:
  - 11-corner -FU/-FE matrix: baseline 4/11 -> fixed 11/11, every success RUN
    and not merely linked, and both must-refuse corners still refusing.
  - full tests/test corpus, 1981 tests: 1981 SAME, 0 DIFF.
  - self-host fixpoint stage3 == stage4 byte-identical (this md5); the
    stage2->stage3 delta was exactly two bytes of embedded build date.
  This is also the exact binary that cross-built the v55 Win64 ppcx64.exe.

STILL ON v54 AFTER THIS RELEASE
  aarch64-linux, arm-linux, arm-linux-cross, i386-linux-cross, x86_64-darwin
  and aarch64-darwin all still ship the pre-fix v54 compiler and therefore
  still refuse a missing -FU/-FE directory.  Each needs a cross rebuild from
  eae5d3e919; that is tracked and not yet done.  Nothing about those packages
  is mis-stated -- they are honestly labelled v54 -- but do not read this
  release as "the fix is everywhere".
